label: Resilient Well-Connected Graduate Woman
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below typical thresholds, near-minimal depression on the PHQ-9, and virtually negligible anxiety on the GAD-7. The combination of low scores across all three mental health dimensions suggests a stable, socially connected, and emotionally resilient group.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, spending 1–3 hours of daily screen/online time
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.82), indicating strong social connectedness and satisfaction with relationships
Near-floor depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.28), suggesting minimal to no depressive burden
Extremely low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03), reflecting an almost complete absence of anxiety concerns
Moderate and controlled daily screen or online usage (1–3 hours), potentially reflecting balanced digital habits
Highly educated (graduate or above), which may contribute to greater access to coping resources and social support
tone: Calm, stable, and emotionally grounded — reflecting a respondent group that experiences minimal psychological distress and maintains strong social and emotional well-being

label: High-Distress Digitally Immersed Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.67), PHQ-9 depression score (1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.16) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. The cluster is moderately sized (n = 179), indicating a meaningful subgroup rather than an outlier pattern.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness despite extended time online
Endorses frequent depressive symptoms (elevated PHQ-9 mean of 1.73)
Exhibits the highest distress on anxiety measures (GAD-7 mean of 2.16)
Heavy digital engagement (more than 5 hours daily) co-occurs with psychological distress
Highly educated yet experiencing significant emotional difficulties
tone: Concerned and empathetic; the data point to a vulnerable subgroup whose high educational attainment and extensive digital connectivity do not buffer against substantial emotional distress.

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.23, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.80, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating generally positive mental well-being.
